slides.title: Induction machine - Overview o Commutatorless motor drives offer a number of advantages over conventional DC motor drive
slides.body:
DC motor drives for electric propulsion, as low cost, high power factor, reliable
operation.
o An AC induction motor is one of the simplest and most reliable types of electric
AC motor, with the power ranging from a few watts to many kilowatts.
o There are many different ways to design and control such motors, from low
cost with a single-phase input to high accuracy with a polyphase approach, and
this type of system is the most widely used motor across the consumer and
industrial markets.

slides.title: Induction motor – Structure
Induction motor – Working principle
slides.body:
The stator of a three-phase induction machine contains a series of
windings to which three-phase electrical power is applied.
These windings establish a rotating magnetic field in the air gap
between the stator and the rotor. The stator field can be seen as a
series of north-south poles revolving around the circumference of
the stator.
The rotation of the stator magnetic field occurs at a fixed speed
called synchronous speed and linked to the supply frequency f.
In IMs, the angular speed of the rotor is lower than the
synchronous speed of the magnetic field generated by the
stator windings, hence called asynchronous.

slides.title: Induction motor – Working principle
slides.body:
The rotor windings are immersed in this rotating magnetic
field. Since the rotor turns slower than the stator field, the
magnetic flux linkage in the rotor windings varies.
The rotating magnetic field induces currents in the
rotor by magnetic induction (Faraday's law).
These induced currents, in turn, generate a rotor
magnetic field, which opposes flux variations; it interacts
with the stator field, generating a torque on the rotor
windings which causes the rotor to rotate.

slides.title: IM - Modeling
Torque – speed relationship
slides.body:
At synchronous speed, no torque is produced by
the motor, because no current is induced in the rotor
windings.
If the rotor rotates at a lower speed than the stator field,
the motor runs in motoring mode . Otherwise, the
motor operates in generator mode . The maximum
torque, which can be obtained at the motor shaft, is
called pullout torque . The nominal torque is
conventionally half of the pullout torque. The motor
usually operates in the linear region between the
positive and the negative nominal torque.

slides.title: Control strategies – V/f
slides.body:
In the past, mainly the rather simple voltage-to-frequency (V/f) control was used and it can still be
found in industrial drives. This method is a scalar method, that is, it operates just on the module (and
not the phase) of the control quantities involved. The main drawback is its limited dynamic
performance.

slides.title: Control strategies - FOC
slides.body:
Another control strategy for inverter-fed variable-speed drives is the “Field Oriented Control” (FOC).
The time-dependent instantaneous three-phase system values, such as currents and voltages, are
transformed into an orthogonal two-dimensional coordinate system by means of the Park
transformation. This coordinate system rotates with the same frequency as the three-phase values.
From this, the three AC quantities are reduced to two DC quantities which, in general, are much
simpler to control. The two DC quantities can be represented as a “space vector” in the two-dimensional
coordinate system. This transformation results in a controllability of torque of the induction machine that
is similar to the DC machine.

slides.title: Control strategies - FOC
slides.body:
This technique controls the variable of interest in module
and phase with the aim of separating, as occurs in the
direct current machine, the current components that
contribute to the flux and torque. With this type of
regulation it is possible to obtain rapid response and
good adaptation by the machine, whose operation,
moreover, can be extended to the four quadrants.

slides.title: Control strategies - FOC
Inverter
slides.body:
Inverters for induction motors are generally classified into
voltage-fed and current-fed types. Because of the need of a large
series inductance to emulate a current source, the current-fed
inverters are rarely used for EV propulsion. In fact, the voltage-fed
inverters are almost exclusively used because they are very
simple and can have power flow in either direction.
Control strategies can be classified as:
- PWM (Pulse Width Modulation);
- Six-step.

slides.title: Inverter
slides.body:
The inverter design highly depends on the technology of power
devices. Nowadays, the insulated-gate bipolar transistor
(IGBT)-based inverter is most attractive and has been widely
accepted by modern EVs. The selection of power devices is based
on:
- the voltage rating is at least twice the nominal battery voltage;
- the current rating is large enough so that there is no need to
connect several power devices in parallel;
- the switching speed is sufficiently high to suppress motor
harmonics and acoustic noise.

slides.title: Sinusoidal PWM control
slides.body:
When the value assumed by one of the
modulators exceeds that of the triangular carrier,
the switch S of the corresponding phase is
turned on while when the value assumed by one
of the modulators is less than that of the
triangular carrier it is turned off (and the other
switch of the same branch is turned on).
The technique can be implemented either in an
analog or digital way.

slides.title: Six-step inverter control
slides.body:
In 6-step (or square wave) operation, the switch is alternately
closed and open for a time equal to T/2, where T is the period of
the alternating output voltage.
The switches of the same branch are controlled in a
complementary way.

slides.title: Six-step inverter control
slides.body:
In 6-step operation, each switch changes state every T/2, while the
inverter changes state every T/6.
It is called a 6-step inverter since the waveform is built in the 6
sixths of the period. Every sixth of a period, the components that
are commanded for switching change.
Furthermore, in period T the inverter assumes 6 different states:
(101), (100), (110), (010), (011), (001). These are called active
states.
The amplitude of the output voltage depends only on V CC and the
state of the switches.

slides.title: Induction machine
slides.body:
Because of high cost, need for maintenance, and lack of sturdiness,
the wound-rotor induction motor is less attractive than the
squirrel-cage counterpart, especially for electric propulsion in electric
vehicles (EVs). Hence, the squirrel-cage induction motor is loosely
named as the induction motor for EV propulsion.
In addition to the common advantages of commutatorless motor
drives, the induction motor drives possess the definite advantages of
low cost and ruggedness. These advantages can generally
outweigh their major disadvantage of control complexity and
facilitate this technology being widely accepted for EVs.
